land.text: Lycia, 'awarded to Rhodes in the Peace of Apamea in 188 BC' and taken back by Rome in 168 BC

predecessors.note: The rhodes dossier dates Rhodes' loss of Lycia to 167 (Rhodian Peraia page); the Lycia and Lycian League pages say 168.

land.text: Lycia, annexed by Claudius in 43 AD; joined with Pamphylia as Lycia et Pamphylia by Vespasian in 74

successors.note: Province of Lycia from 43, Lycia et Pamphylia from 74.

capitals.name: Xanthos
capitals.note: The Lycia page names Xanthos as the Lycian capital but gives no meeting place for the League's general assembly; the six largest cities were Xanthos, Patara, Pinara, Olympos, Myra and Tlos.

correction.text: Lycia on the Teke Peninsula: the 23 cities of the League, 'granted autonomy as a protectorate of Rome in 168 BC'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row; Cliopatria's Rhodes shape of 188-165 holds Lycia and Caria south of the Maeander). The pages give no area and no boundary: Lycia is the region, the Teke Peninsula. The League is said to have 23 cities (Strabo) and Cibyra's tetrapolis sat beside it; whether the Cibyratis was in the League's land is not settled by the pages.

region.text: Lycia, twenty-three cities in a general assembly

ledger.note: 168: Rome frees Lycia from Rhodes and the Lycian League stands as a protectorate. 'granted autonomy as a protectorate of Rome in 168 BC'; 'the Roman Republic gave Lycia to Rhodes for 20 years, taking it back in 168 BC'. The League is 'first known from two inscriptions of the early 2nd century BC', so it may be older than 168 (the Lycian League page leaves that open).

region.text: Lycia, as Rhodes held it from 188

ledger.note: 168: Lycia leaves Rhodian rule. 'awarded to Rhodes in the Peace of Apamea in 188 BC' and taken back in 168; the senate decree of 169 'gave the Carians and the Lycians their freedom' (the page gives 169, 168 and 167-168 in different passages).

region.text: the League and its cities, autonomous under Roman protection

ledger.note: 168: Lycia is a protectorate of Rome. 'granted autonomy as a protectorate of Rome in 168 BC'; later inscriptions give 'peace and loyal alliance between the People of the Romans and the cities of Lycia', and Caesar's treaty of 46 BC begins 'Friendship, alliance and peace both by land and sea in perpetuity'.

region.text: Xanthos, the largest city of the League, besieged by Brutus

ledger.note: 42: Brutus comes to Lycia for money before Philippi and besieges Xanthos after the League refused to contribute. 'In 42 BC, during the Liberators' civil war, Brutus came to Lycia to obtain funds before the Battle of Philippi.' The page dates the arrival, not the siege; the occupation ends with the same campaign, the same year (page silent on months). Counterpart: Brutus's Liberators' faction, the roman-republic dossier's string for 43-42 (reviewer me-05-x, 2026-10-19; was roman-republic).
42: Brutus leaves Lycia for Philippi (page silent on the end of the occupation; the city was 'rebuilt under Mark Antony', undated).

27 BC: the Roman side of the protectorate passes from the Republic to the Principate. Page silent: the League pages give no change of overlord; bridged from the Roman constitutional date, as for Cappadocia.
27 BC: Lycia is a free ally of the Roman Empire under Augustus (page silent; bridging).
43: Claudius ends the protectorate. 'In 43 AD the emperor Claudius annexed Lycia'; Cassius Dio says he 'reduced the Lycians to servitude because they had revolted'.

43: Lycia becomes a Roman province. 'In 43 AD the emperor Claudius annexed Lycia'; the Lycia page says Claudius 'dissolved the league', the Lycian League page that the League was retained after annexation, and Vespasian joined Lycia and Pamphylia in 74.
43: the Lycian League ends as an independent state. The Lycia et Pamphylia page: 'In 43 AD, the emperor Claudius had annexed Lycia'; the merged province is 'Established: 74' (Vespasian).

wars.name: Brutus's Lycian campaign
wars.outcome: Brutus came to Lycia 'to obtain funds before the Battle of Philippi' and 'besieged Xanthos after the Lycian League refused to contribute'; the page gives the city 'rebuilt under Mark Antony' without a year.
wars.note: The siege and its result are not dated beyond the year; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Lycian revolt and the annexation of Lycia
wars.outcome: Claudius annexed Lycia in 43 AD; Cassius Dio, quoted on the Lycian League page, says he 'reduced the Lycians to servitude because they had revolted'.
wars.note: The page gives no year or place for the revolt itself.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier for the League; Lycia is drawn as the Teke Peninsula region.

sources.title: Lycian League
sources.note: Formation, 23 cities and votes, Rhodes 188-168, protectorate 168, Roman treaties, Claudius 43.

sources.title: Lycia
sources.note: Rhodian control 188-168, the 169/168 decree, Xanthos as capital, Claudius 43, Vespasian 74.

sources.title: Lycia et Pamphylia
sources.note: Annexation 43, province established 74; silent on the League.

sources.title: Xanthos
sources.note: Brutus in Lycia, 42 BC; the only dated sentence on the siege.

notes: Four pages (budget 2-5). Gaps: the First Mithridatic War (88-84) and the Second (83-81, Murena deposing Moagetes at Cibyra) are not dated on the Lycian pages for the League's own land; Cibyra's tetrapolis is not settled as League land; the page contradicts itself on whether the League survived 43 (Lycia: 'dissolved the league'; Lycian League: retained). Start year -168 follows the Lycia page ('taking it back in 168 BC'); the rhodes dossier has the loss of Lycia in 167 to 'nobody' (Rhodian Peraia page) and should name lycian-league as counterpart. Region 'Lycia' resolves in the gazetteer (74 cells, bbox 27.3-30.5 E, confidence 2; it reaches west of the Teke Peninsula into Caria, so a renderer may want it trimmed to the Teke Peninsula); the place names Xanthos, Patara, Myra, Tlos, Pinara and Olympos are missing from places.jsonl, so Xanthos is a coordinate radius. The vassal pair uses roman-republic and roman-empire as counterparts in the League's own ledger (the convention used by kingdom-of-cappadocia). No rulers strip: the Lyciarch is named by Strabo but no list is given. The occupation of Xanthos (42) is a single campaign year.
